A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CD-RLHF work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, GPT-4 and human evaluations, and case studies of CD-RLHF.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds broader Sent-Rewards comparisons and GPT-4 alignment-quality results in Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: The ICM architecture, prediction-error reward, top-k gating, whitening, and PPO algorithm remain unchanged. The new action-embedding notation and expanded explanations clarify operations already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions cover TL;DR summarization, UltraFeedback instruction following, MT-Bench, and ROC story generation. The added GPT-4 quality evaluation reuses existing tasks and datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands Sent-Rewards from Gemma-2B comparisons to Gemma-7B, Llama-3.2-1B, and Llama-3.2-3B on both datasets. This fills the comparator gap across most model configurations in the main evaluation. New Table 6 also compares CD-RLHF against SFT and RLHF on alignment quality.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces GPT-4 alignment evaluation of Llama-3.2-3B using the highest-reward response from ten candidates, with task-specific judging criteria in Appendix B.1. Table 6 reports 50 decisions per comparison. Existing training and diversity-evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The KL and temperature ablations, intrinsic-reward frequency analysis, training curves, MT-Bench analysis, top-k study, and case studies are retained. The new alignment table adds performance evaluation rather than an ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Run and seed disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, including existing plotted error bars and shaded curves. No uncertainty estimates or significance tests accompany the added comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds six Sent-Rewards result rows, substantially extending the comparison evidence. These include Gemma-7B TL;DR Diversity of 0.1447 versus CD-RLHF's retained 0.1360. New Table 6 reports CD-RLHF versus RLHF wins/ties/losses of 27/0/23 on TL;DR and 21/7/22 on UltraFeedback, plus comparisons against SFT. Previously reported benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is retained. Numbered equations and the new action-embedding and Top-k notation restate existing operations; no substantive definition, derivation, assumption, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the claims of improved lexical and semantic diversity with RLHF-comparable alignment and stronger MT-Bench generalization. The added evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: The UltraFeedback discussion changes from interpreting Sent-Rewards as a higher-quality/lower-diversity trade-off to describing partial diversity mitigation. New Appendix C.1 interprets alignment as comparable to RLHF, but Table 6's superiority caption overstates the UltraFeedback result of 21 wins versus 22 losses. Existing limitations retain their meaning.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 and new Table 5 document Sent-Rewards' entropy weight of 0.01 and model-specific SelfBLEU/SentBERT weights. Appendix B.1 adds exact quality-judging prompts. The entropy disclosure does not establish that existing experiments were rerun; retained Gemma-2B scores and previously specified weights are unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists and research positioning are unchanged. Removing the Pathak et al. citation from the abstract does not remove that work, which remains cited and discussed elsewhere.

P1.justification: Section 3.2.2 receives localized rewriting and descriptive headings clarifying state representations, ICM training, gating, and whitening. Other changes include grammar edits and subdivision of Appendix C; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised token examples and clearer gating, and Figure 2 updates representation labels. Table 1 expands and moves; two tables and quality-prompt boxes are added. Existing plots and appendix examples are retained within the same overall layout.

improvement.justification: Expanded Sent-Rewards comparisons and disclosed reward weights improve comparison completeness and reproducibility. Clearer method exposition and the additional GPT-4 evaluation also help assess the alignment claim. The gains are limited by the best-of-10 evaluation scope and overstatement in Table 6's caption, which claims superiority despite 21 wins and 22 losses against RLHF on UltraFeedback. Overall, the added evidence provides a modest net improvement.
